Patch Set 1:

Hi all,

> Do you have any opinions on how to proceed here?

Most of the discussion on getting actual MCTP-based infrastructure into OpenBMC is happening in the MCTP daemon design discussion:

https://gerrit.openbmc-project.xyz/c/openbmc/docs/+/20420

This change req seems to sidestep that a little; I'd imagine that the nvme sensors would use the infrastructure introduced by that design, instead of using libmctp directly.

That said, we still have the fork issue. I'm happy to move libmctp to under openbmc/ if that makes things easier. Any objections to that?

I was unaware of that discussion, I will try to weigh in on the review.  With that said, in our experience with IPMB, which follows a similar path to what's being suggested, the added dbus traffic of a bridge tends to very quickly overwhelm the BMCs CPU resources.  This is fine for IPMB, as there's 2-3 clients in a given system, and we can simply reduce scan rates to once every 3 seconds make it more capable, but MCTP (for the NVMe use case) has more stringent needs around throughput.  Namely, there are systems that have 24 NVMe drives on a single i2c "bus", behind multiple muxes that need to be scanned on 1-2 second intervals.  Our expectation was that, given the performance we're seeing out of IPMB, a dbus->MCTP bridge was not going to cut it.  With that said, some members of our Poland team did build an example for testing performance characteristics of this mechanism, that I've just got my hands on this morning.  I will try to make that code available once I've pieced through it.

> 
> That said, we still have the fork issue. I'm happy to move libmctp to under openbmc/ if that makes things easier. Any objections to that?

I don't have a strong opinion where libmctp lives repo-wise.  I would like the changes code reviewed, and have a mechanism for pushing reviews.  If we want to use github for that, great, I can get Nikhil to open reviews for the changes he's made.  The logical place to me seemed to be openbmc/ but I'm open to other possibilities.
